title: Two Tribes Ask to Stay Behind
overview: The tribes of Reuben and Gad ask to settle in good grazing land east of the Jordan River, and Moses agrees only after they promise to help the other tribes fight for their land to the west.

parts.label: A request for grazing land (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: Reuben and Gad owned huge herds, and the land east of the Jordan, recently taken in war from the Amorite kings, was ideal pasture. They ask to settle there instead of crossing the river with everyone else.

parts.label: Moses fears a repeat (vv. 6-15)
parts.note: Moses hears their request as a refusal to share the coming war. He recalls the scouting trip from Kadesh, when a discouraging report turned the people back and that generation, except Caleb and Joshua, died during forty years in the wilderness, and he warns the same could happen again.

parts.label: The tribes offer a deal (vv. 16-27)
parts.note: They propose to repair the towns for their families and herds, then send their armed men ahead of the other tribes until everyone has land. Moses agrees but warns that breaking this promise would be a wrong against God, and that it would catch up with them.

parts.label: The deal made official (vv. 28-32)
parts.note: Moses lays out the exact terms to Eleazar the priest, Joshua and the heads of the tribes, and Reuben and Gad agree to them again. If the two tribes fight, they keep the eastern land; if not, they must take land west of the river like everyone else.

parts.label: Land handed out and resettled (vv. 33-42)
parts.note: Moses gives the conquered kingdoms of Sihon and Og to Reuben, Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh, though the text never says why Manasseh is now included. The tribes rebuild and rename towns, possibly to remove names honoring other gods such as Nebo and Baal, and clans of Manasseh capture more Amorite settlements by force.

think: Once you have secured what you need, what do you think you still owe to people who are only now facing the hard part?
